text: I would look at, do the co-founders get along? Are these people committed? Do they really know about their product? Do they care? Are they going to quit their job?
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica to explain her "Social Radar" nickname at Y Combinator and how her evaluation approach differed from her technical co-founders. Jessica explains that while her three co-founders (Paul Graham, Robert Morris, and Trevor Blackwell) focused on technical aspects during 10-minute founder interviews, she concentrated on interpersonal dynamics and behavioral cues. She would observe whether co-founders worked well together, if founders were truly committed to their ideas, and whether they would actually quit their day jobs to pursue their startups full-time.
text_ko: 저라면 먼저 공동창업자들(co-founders)이 사이가 잘 맞는지 볼 거예요. 이 사람들이 얼마나 헌신적인지, 제품(product)을 진짜로 잘 아는지, 관심을 가지고 있는지, 그리고 직장을 그만두고 이 일에 전념할 생각이 있는지도 확인해요.
text_zh: 我会看：联合创始人(co-founders)合得来吗？这些人有没有真正投入？他们真的了解自己的产品吗？他们在乎这件事吗？会不会辞掉现在的工作？
text_es: Me fijaría en: ¿los cofundadores (co-founders) se llevan bien? ¿Están comprometidos? ¿Conocen de verdad su producto? ¿Les importa? ¿Van a dejar sus empleos?
key_sentence: Do they really know about their product?
original_text: I would look at, do the co-founders get along? Are these people committed? Do they really know about their product? Do they care? Are they going to quit their job? Or are they telling us that they are going to quit their job, but really aren't? All these little social cues that I'd try to pick up on.

text: If a founder would get defensive, that was always a bad sign, always a bad sign.
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica about specific red flags she would look for during Y Combinator interviews. Jessica explains that defensiveness was a major warning sign because successful startups require founders who can handle criticism and questioning from customers, investors, and users. She valued founders who remained open-minded when challenged and could engage in productive dialogue rather than becoming defensive when their ideas were questioned.
text_ko: 창업자가 방어적으로 나오면 그건 항상 안 좋은 신호예요, 정말 항상 그래요.
text_zh: 如果创始人一有防备心，那就是个坏迹象，始终如此。
text_es: Siempre que un fundador se ponía a la defensiva, era una mala señal. Siempre.
key_sentence: that was always a bad sign, always a bad sign.
original_text: If a founder would get defensive, that was always a bad sign, always a bad sign. The best founders would say, "Gosh, I have thought about it and here's what I figured out." Or, they just have this almost a tennis match and a conversation rather than closing up and feeling like, oh, this person's interrogating me.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a protective or guarded attitude, often in response to criticism or perceived threats.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being defensive can indicate a reluctance to accept feedback or adapt to constructive criticism, which may hinder growth and collaboration.
vocabulary.nuance: While a defensive stance may arise from a desire to protect one's ideas, it can also signal insecurity or a lack of openness to improvement.

text: I remember specifically Joe brought out the cereal boxes, the Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's, and I just thought, oh my God, they're going to work hard to do whatever they can to make this company succeed.
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica to share the famous Airbnb interview story. Jessica explains that during the 2009 financial crisis, Y Combinator was being very selective and only funding scrappy founders who could survive on little money. The Airbnb founders (Brian Chesky, Joe Gebbia, and Nate Blecharczyk) came in with tremendous energy, though Y Combinator actually hated their idea of staying in someone's airbed. At the end of the interview, Joe showed them cereal boxes they had created - Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's - made by repackaging generic cereals, which demonstrated their resourcefulness and determination.
text_ko: 특히 기억나는 건 조가 'Obama O's'랑 'Cap'n McCain's' 시리얼 박스를 꺼냈을 때예요. 그때 저는 '세상에, 이 사람들 이 회사를 성공시키려고 뭐든지 열심히 할 거구나' 하고 생각했어요.
text_zh: 我记得Joe专门拿出那些麦片盒子，什么奥巴马麦片(Obama O's)、麦凯恩船长麦片(Cap'n McCain's)之类的，我当时就想，天哪，这帮人真是拼了，为了让公司成功什么招都使得出来。
text_es: Recuerdo específicamente cuando Joe sacó las cajas de cereal, los Obama O's y los Cap'n McCain's, y pensé "Dios mío, esta gente va a darlo todo para que la empresa triunfe."
key_sentence: They brought out cereal boxes, going to great lengths for success.

vocabulary.definition: To achieve a desired aim or result; to accomplish one's goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'succeed' often refers to reaching specific performance metrics, such as profitability, market share, or successful product launches.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'succeed' implies a positive outcome, it can also carry the weight of expectations and pressures to continuously perform well.

text: Earnestness is one of the most important because earnest, sort of to me, is bucketed with authenticity.
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica about additional qualities she looks for in founders beyond being hustlers and having domain expertise. Jessica introduces the concept of "earnestness" as one of the most critical traits for successful founders. She explains that earnestness goes hand-in-hand with authenticity - founders must genuinely care about the problems they're solving and the users they're serving, rather than just pursuing startups because it's trendy or they think an idea is cool.
text_ko: 진지함은 가장 중요한 것들 중 하나예요. 제게 진지함은 어떻게 보면 진정성과 같은 범주에 속해요.
text_zh: 真诚很重要，在我看来，真诚（earnestness）某种程度上就和真实性（authenticity）放一块儿的。
text_es: La sinceridad es una de las cosas más importantes; digamos que, para mí, va en el mismo saco (bucketed) que la autenticidad.
key_sentence: Earnestness is bucketed with authenticity, key to success for founders.
original_text: Earnestness is one of the most important because earnest, sort of to me, is bucketed with authenticity. And to be a successful startup founder, you have to care so much about the problem you're trying to solve, the users you're serving and being earnest about it is so key to success.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being genuine, real, and true to one's own character or values.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, authenticity is crucial for building trust with customers and stakeholders, as it reflects a company's commitment to transparency and integrity.
vocabulary.nuance: While authenticity is generally viewed positively, it can be misinterpreted as a lack of professionalism if not balanced with appropriate business conduct.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being serious, sincere, and determined in intention or effort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business environment, earnestness is valued as it reflects a commitment to goals and a genuine approach to teamwork and client relations.
vocabulary.nuance: Although earnestness is generally seen as a positive trait, it can sometimes be perceived as overly intense or lacking in levity, depending on the context.

text: You sort of need that desperation like, "I have to make this startup succeed because it's my job." Not like, "Oh, I'll just stay at Google." You need that. And we found that founders who weren't leaving their jobs, it was just not working out.
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica to elaborate on what "commitment" means when evaluating founders. Jessica explains the concept of "burning the boat" - founders need to fully commit by quitting their day jobs because having a safety net often prevents them from pushing through the inevitable difficult periods of building a startup. She notes that Y Combinator discovered that founders who kept their jobs at companies like Google would typically abandon their startups when challenges arose, since they had the security of their regular paycheck and benefits.
text_ko: 어느 정도 "'이 스타트업(startup)을 꼭 성공시켜야 해요, 이건 제 일이에요' 하는 절박함이 필요해요. '아, 그냥 구글에 남아있을래요' 식이면 안 돼요. 그리고 저희가 보니까 직장을 그만두지 않는 창업자들(founders)은 잘 안 되더라고요.
text_zh: 你得有那种desperate的感觉，就是"我必须让这个创业公司成功，因为这就是我的饭碗。"而不是"哦，不行我就回谷歌待着。"你必须要有这种心态。我们发现那些不辞职的创始人，基本上都做不成。
text_es: Necesitas como esa desesperación de "tengo que hacer que este startup funcione porque es mi trabajo." No como "ah, me quedo en Google y ya." Eso es fundamental. Y nos dimos cuenta de que los fundadores que no dejaban sus trabajos, simplemente no les funcionaba.
key_sentence: You sort of need that desperation for your startup to succeed.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who establish or create a company or organization, often taking on significant risks and responsibilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founders are typically the visionaries who drive the initial concept and strategy, often influencing the company's culture and direction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'founders' carries a connotation of innovation and entrepreneurship, and is often associated with a sense of ownership and personal investment in the venture's success.

vocabulary.definition: To achieve a desired aim or result, often after considerable effort or struggle.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, succeeding typically refers to reaching key milestones such as profitability, market share, or successful product launches, which are critical for attracting investment and scaling operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'succeed' generally implies a positive outcome, it can also suggest the culmination of various trials and setbacks, highlighting the challenges inherent in entrepreneurial endeavors.

text: I spent hours and hours on the phone with people, with my girlfriends, dissecting situations, and then all through high school, and college, I mean the amount of time we wasted discussing social matters with people, and boys, and things like that.
speaker: Jessica Livingston
context: Lenny asks Jessica when she first noticed her social radar abilities and whether they were developed or innate. Jessica reflects on her childhood and explains that she's always been fascinated by understanding people's motivations and social dynamics. She describes how even as a young person, she would spend countless hours analyzing interpersonal situations with friends, which she now realizes was early training for her ability to read people and understand what drives them.
text_ko: 친구들이랑 전화로 몇 시간이고 상황을 샅샅이 분석하며 보냈어요. 그게 고등학교 때부터 대학 때까지 쭉 이어졌고요. 사람 관계나 남자 얘기 같은 것들로 수다 떨며 얼마나 많은 시간을 낭비했는지 몰라요.
text_zh: 我跟朋友，尤其是闺蜜们，经常为了各种事电话聊上好几个小时，琢磨各种情况。从高中到大学，光是跟别人、跟男生聊这些社交上的事儿，我们就浪费了好多时间。
text_es: Pasé horas y horas al teléfono con gente, con mis amigas, desmenuzando situaciones, y luego, durante todo el instituto y la universidad… qué cantidad de tiempo perdimos hablando de la vida social, de chicos y de cosas por el estilo.
key_sentence: I spent frightening hours dissecting situations, genuinely interested in social matters.
original_text: I spent hours and hours on the phone with people, with my girlfriends, dissecting situations, and then all through high school, and college, I mean the amount of time we wasted discussing social matters with people, and boys, and things like that. It was just frightening how much time I wasted, but I just was genuinely interested in it.

vocabulary.definition: To dissect means to analyze something in detail, often by breaking it down into its components for better understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, dissecting can refer to the thorough analysis of market trends, financial reports, or project outcomes to derive insights and improve decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While dissecting often implies a careful and methodical approach, it can also carry a negative connotation if it suggests over-analysis or excessive scrutiny.

vocabulary.definition: Social matters refer to issues or topics that pertain to society, relationships, and interpersonal dynamics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, social matters can influence workplace culture, employee engagement, and corporate social responsibility initiatives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a focus on the human element within business, highlighting the importance of relationships and community.
